newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy court hears challenge to Priebke judge.
newsitem.headline: Italy court hears challenge to Priebke judge.

text.p: Italy's highest appeal court met on Tuesday to consider whether to nullify a controversial verdict that former SS captain Erich Priebke should not be jailed for war crimes.

The Court of Cassation sat for two hours to hear a request from the prosecution and lawyers for civil plaintiffs to overturn a lower court's rejection of a previous challenge to the impartiality of the presiding judge, Agostino Quistelli.
If the petition is admitted the verdict could be scrapped and the trial would have to start again with different judges. A ruling was expected to be announced later on Tuesday, court sources said.
Priebke, 83, was tried by an Italian military court on charges of involvement in the Nazi massacre of 335 men and boys at the Ardeatine Caves outside Rome in March 1944.
The trial ended on August 1 with a verdict finding him guilty but ordering him freed because the statute of limitations for his crimes had run out.

The German, who had lived openly for almost 50 years in Argentina, was blocked inside the courthouse by angry protesters and re-arrested hours later when Germany said it intended to extradite him for a war crimes trial there.
He is now being held on remand at Rome's Regina Coeli jail.

The Ardeatine Caves massacre, ordered in reprisal for a partisan bomb attack on German soldiers in Rome, was the worst atrocity committed in Italy in World War Two. Seventy-five of the victims were Jews.
Priebke admitted shooting two people and checking off names from a list at the caves, but his lawyers argued he should not be held responsible because he had to follow orders.
Priebke was extradited to Italy from Argentina last November.
